title: Derived functions on a free representable module as sheafified derived sections
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site, small in the sheaf universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with finite products and a subcanonical topology, meaning that every representable $h_P(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(V,P)$ is a sheaf. Let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings and use ordinary sheaves of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $U$ for forgetting an $R$-module sheaf to its abelian sheaf, $\iota:\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{PAb}(\mathcal C)$ for inclusion into abelian presheaves, and $a$ for abelian sheafification, the left adjoint of $\iota$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Use cochain derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with $D^+$ denoting the full subcategory of objects whose cohomology vanishes in all sufficiently negative degrees. The functor $R\iota:D^+(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C))\to D^+(\operatorname{PAb}(\mathcal C))$ is computed by applying $\iota$ to bounded-below injective resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. For $P\in\mathcal C$, let $R[P]$ be the free $R$-module sheaf on $h_P$, that is, the sheafification of $V\mapsto\bigoplus_{h_P(V)}R(V)$, and put $H_P=\mathcal Hom_R(R[P],-)$ with sheaf Hom as in [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Derive $H_P$ in its second variable by nonnegative injective resolutions of module sheaves. Let $t_P$ be exact precomposition on abelian presheaves with $V\mapsto V\times P$, so $(t_P A)(V)=A(V\times P)$. For every $R$-module sheaf $M$ there is a canonical isomorphism
$$D(U)RH_P(M[0])\ \cong\ D(a)D(t_P)R\iota(UM[0])\quad\text{in }D^+(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C)).$$
It is natural covariantly in $M$ and contravariantly in $P$. Its degree-zero normalization is the canonical identification $H_P(M)(V)=M(V\times P)$: a section is evaluated on the universal generator of the free module after restriction to the slice over $V$. The isomorphism takes the map induced by any module morphism $M\to N$ to $D(a)D(t_P)R\iota$ of its underlying abelian morphism. It is also an isomorphism in the ordinary unbounded derived category under the canonical inclusions of the bounded-below categories. No finite-cover hypothesis on the site, projectivity of $P$, or discreteness of $R$ is assumed.

proof.text: Choose $r:M[0]\to I^\bullet$ and $c_r:Q(\iota UI)\cong R\iota(UM[0])$ by [lem-sfb-module-resolution-derived-presheaf-comparison]. The site is small and $R$ is a commutative ring sheaf, as that lemma requires. By [lem-sfb-free-representable-slice-evaluation], $H_P$ is additive left exact and $UH_P(I)\cong a t_P\iota UI$ as complexes, with coefficient and parameter naturality. Finite products and subcanonicity are among the present hypotheses.

source.place: Tag 03EM (lemma-internal-hom), its localized-Hom definition and free-generator specialization; module sheafification and localization in lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules and definition-localize-ringed-site. Agent formulation with explicit inverse and naturality.

proof.text: The exactness of $U$ is [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], and exactness of $a$ is [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact]. Exact evaluation [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-presheaves-evaluation-exact] makes $t_P$ exact, since its value at $V$ is evaluation at $V\times P$. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] represents $D(U),D(a),D(t_P)$ termwise. By [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective], $H_P(I)$ represents $RH_P(M[0])$. Composing the complex isomorphism of step 1 with $D(a)D(t_P)(c_r)$ gives the required derived isomorphism.

For $f:M\to N$, [lem-sfb-module-resolution-derived-presheaf-comparison] supplies an augmentation-compatible lift $\widetilde f$, unique up to homotopy, and $c_{r'}Q(\iota U\widetilde f)=R\iota(Uf[0])c_r$. The chain-map naturality of [lem-sfb-free-representable-slice-evaluation] and the natural termwise comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] now make the assembled square commute. Additivity preserves $f-g=dh+hd$, so the derived map is independent of the lift. Taking $f=\mathrm{id}$ proves resolution independence. For $u:P'\to P$, the slice lemma identifies the complex map with restriction along $1_V\times u$; $c_r$ is a presheaf-derived map, so the same square commutes.

source.place: Tag 03FD (lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree), acyclicity proof; derived.tex Tag 015E (lemma-leray-acyclicity), Tag 013P (lemma-morphisms-lift), Tag 013S (lemma-morphisms-equal-up-to-homotopy). Agent formulation as a normalized isomorphism of derived presheaves.

proof.text: All representatives are nonnegative. On degree-zero kernels $c_r$ is the identity by [lem-sfb-module-resolution-derived-presheaf-comparison], and the complex comparison is generator evaluation by [lem-sfb-free-representable-slice-evaluation]. Exactness of $a,t_P$ from step 2 therefore gives exactly the stated normalization. Applying the canonical inclusions $D^+\to D$, viewed as full subcategories in the statement, preserves the isomorphism and its commuting squares. None of the steps uses an extra site or coefficient hypothesis.

reviewed_lean.note: Node changes only the lean field; statement verbatim matches file. Objects: ring = forget₂ of CommRingCat sheaf, modules = ringedSiteModules, free = sheafified PresheafOfModules.free∘yoneda with generator via sheafification unit, H_P = SheafOfModules.homFunctor (def-pur-sheaf-hom), t_P = whiskering by (−×P).op, U/ι/a = toSheaf/sheafToPresheaf/presheafToSheaf. leftComplex = U H_P on module-injective resolution, rightComplex = a t_P ι on abelian-injective resolution of UM (no claim that U preserves injectives); E is a D⁺ isomorphism (not per-degree), pinned by E.hom = Q(comparisonMap θ c) for every augmentation-compatible c, with c's existence asserted; θ pinned by generator evaluation at Over.mk fst on gen(snd). Coefficient naturality (all s, t lifts; f=id gives independence of resolutions) and contravariant P-naturality (free.map f vs restriction along 1×f) checked true via 013S homotopy uniqueness and an explicit generator computation; quasi-iso via 03FD acyclicity + 015E. Unbounded clause = Plus.ι.mapIso. Hypotheses: finite products and subcanonical, nothing more; common universe u per size convention. Gates: no hollow defs, only sorry, source and blueprint docstrings with the nine proof steps, all imports present in side-live, citer unaffected.
